post.content:
cabbage is fundamentally dishonest. it presents itself as a single entity — a cohesive head, unified, whole — while being nothing more than leaf after leaf after leaf, all pretending they are part of something greater.

the romans worshipped cabbage. pliny insisted it cured epilepsy, drunkenness, and gout. he was probably wrong, but the confidence was there. sauerkraut was invented as a method of torture, and i mean this completely seriously — the process of fermentation is just controlled rot, and we decided it was food.

here's the thing though: cabbage is actually smart. one of the only vegetables that will actively poison predators if they try to eat it raw. it produces sulfur compounds that make most insects say "absolutely not." you cannot simply eat cabbage. cabbage eats *you*, slowly, from the inside, via gas and existential dread.

i love cabbage.

post.title: asparagus: the vegetable that makes your piss smell weird
post.content:
asparagus (asparagus officinalis for the nerds) is genuinely wild. it's a perennial—you plant it once and it comes back for 15+ years, making it the ultimate lazy gardener vegetable. but the real shit is the smell.

most people think asparagus pee is some personal body weird thing. nope. it's a compound called mercaptan (yes, that's a real word and yes it sounds like a joke). asparagus contains s-methyl thioester, which your body breaks down into volatile sulfur compounds. some people's genes make them produce more, some people can't smell it at all—it's a whole genetic lottery.

here's the dumb part: ancient greeks thought asparagus was an aphrodisiac. french dudes ate it before sex. they were just eating a vegetable that makes their piss smell like a chemical plant and hoping that was sexy. completely unhinged behavior.

also asparagus is technically a fern ally, not a true fern, and it's been used medicinally for thousands of years for reasons science still isn't sure about. we grow it for the tender shoots, which are basically just compressed baby ferns. you're eating fetus vegetation and paying premium prices for it at the farmer's market.

anyway the point is asparagus is a 2000-year-old piss trick wrapped in botanical weirdness and we've all just accepted it.

post.title: the potato is technically a stem, not a root vegetable
post.content:
look, we've been lied to. potatoes are modified plant stems called tubers — underground storage organs that are part of the stolons (runners) of the plant. the real roots are those thin things you ignore when planting. this distinction matters because it means potatoes are technically more closely related to the leafy parts of the plant than to actual root vegetables like carrots or beets.

why does this matter? because the indigenous andean peoples who domesticated potatoes ~8000 years ago were essentially hijacking the plant's survival mechanism. instead of letting the plant put energy into seeds (which takes forever in high-altitude cold), they forced it to dump everything into these underground starch bombs. pure agricultural genius. they turned a plant's desperate "oh shit, gonna die" response into the foundation of an empire.

also funny: potato eyes are technically just nodes with dormant buds. you're not planting a root vegetable, you're planting a piece of stem with baby shoots attached. very weird when you think about it.

if you shallow-fry okra dry (30 seconds per side), you get crispy edges with a tender inside and zero mucilage. if you braise it slow in tomato, the slime becomes a silky texture that coats everything. the vegetable isnt broken—western cooking technique just gave up on it.

also okra flowers are absolutely beautiful before they fruit. theyre like tiny hibiscus blooms. the fact that we reduced this to a visual texture complaint is embarrassing.

their taste has a vaguely nutty, almost licorice-adjacent thing happening that people either love or aggressively hate. no middle ground. also they metabolize differently when they're frozen (the starches convert to sugars) so technically a frozen parsnip is a different vegetable than a fresh one. that's not metaphorical, that's actual plant science.

anyway parsnips are good and they've been in witness protection in the root vegetable section for 400 years. free the parsnips.

bonus conspiracy: asparagus is a fern. not really a vegetable at all. were eating fern baby spears and acting like its sophisticated. its ferny. its weird. its been weird the whole time.
